takeaway: Level II axillary clearance reaches the pectoralis minor, level III the first rib. The thoracodorsal nerve runs along the posterior wall of the axilla.

question.text: During a total mastectomy a consultant performs a level II axillary dissection. Which one of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: The thoracodorsal nerve passes along the posterior wall of the axilla.

lines.text: Here is the axilla, cleared in three levels.
Level one reaches the axillary vein, level two the pectoralis minor, and level three the first rib.
So level two does not reach the first rib or stop at the vein.
During clearance, nerves are at risk, including the sensory intercostobrachial nerve.
The thoracodorsal nerve supplies latissimus dorsi, so protect it.
It passes along the posterior wall of the axilla, that is our answer.
Remember the ladder, and keep the thoracodorsal nerve at the back.
lines.say: (sigh) Remember the ladder, and keep the thoracodorsal nerve at the back.
